subject: City Charter Review
overview: The Governance Committee reviewed proposed charter changes regarding the preamble, general definitions, and the legislative branch. The committee approved several amendments to the draft charter and debated whether the City Council should consist of eleven members (eight ward and three at-large) or nine members (four two-ward districts and five at-large).

items.title: Resolution 24-468: Charter Review - Preamble and Article 1
items.summary: The committee opened discussion on the draft charter's preamble and definitions, questioning the Collins Center representatives on statutory definitions for local news publications.

items.title: Article 2: Legislative Branch - Sections 2-2 to 2-6
items.summary: Approved an amendment to Section 2-3 to ensure council members can communicate directly with city staff without issuing orders, and approved amending Section 2-5 to allow meeting times and places to be set by council rules rather than ordinance.

items.title: Article 2: Legislative Branch - Sections 2-7 to 2-10
items.summary: Approved amendments adding the city messenger position back into the charter, requesting draft language on board residency requirements, and lowering the threshold to reject mayoral appointments from a two-thirds vote to a simple majority.

items.title: Periodic Review of Ordinances (Section 9-6)
items.summary: Approved relocating the periodic ordinance review section into Article 2 as Section 2-11, making the review committee establishable by a vote of the council.

items.title: Section 2-4: Compensation
items.summary: Voted to postpone Section 2-4 to a later meeting to discuss council, mayoral, and school committee compensation together.

items.title: Section 2-1: Council Composition
items.summary: Debated the Charter Study Committee's proposal of an eleven-member council (eight ward, three at-large) versus an amendment for four two-ward districts and five at-large seats, ultimately passing a motion to refer all adopted amendments to a Committee of the Whole meeting.
